docs.title: Python Package Template
docs.text: A Python library template with uv, Pydantic settings, loguru, pytest, Ruff, Git hooks, generated API docs and Conventional Commit releases. Supports Python 3.12–3.14.8.

docs.title: Get started
docs.text:
With Make, Bash, Git and available:

git clone https://github.com/AmineDjeghri/python-package-template.git
cd python-package-template
make install-dev
make run

make help lists all commands.

docs.title: Use the package
docs.text:
Download a wheel from this repository's GitHub Releases, then install that file:

uv pip install "/path/to/python_package_template-<version>-py3-none-any.whl"

from python_package_template.example import hello

hello()

Releases attach a wheel and sdist to GitHub and publish documentation on GitHub Pages; this template does not publish to a package index.

docs.text:
Task Guide Install tools, configure an editor or use Docker Setup Add code or settings Project structure Contribute a change Contributing and conventions Run tests and checks Testing and test map Publish or retry a release Release Start your own package Fork this template

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
1. Follow Setup, then coordinate on an issue.
  2. Branch from dev: feature/<name> or bugfix/<name>.
  3. Update the relevant docs and run make check (Testing).
  4. Open a PR to dev using a Conventional Commit title. PRs are squash-merged; the title determines the version.

See Release for publication and recovery. Coding agents need explicit approval for commits, pushes and publishing. Follow the Code of Conduct; report security issues through SECURITY.md, never a public issue.

docs.title: Reporting a Vulnerability
docs.text:
We take security issues seriously. We appreciate your efforts to responsibly disclose your findings and will make every effort to acknowledge your contributions.

Please do NOT open a public issue or pull request for security vulnerabilities.

To report a security vulnerability privately, use GitHub private vulnerability reporting (preferred):

  • https://github.com/AmineDjeghri/python-package-template/security/advisories/new

For any other question, open an issue to reach the contributors of this repository, but never include vulnerability details in a public issue.

When reporting, please include as much of the following as possible:

  • A description of the vulnerability and its impact
  • The affected component(s) and version(s)
  • Steps to reproduce the issue
  • Any suggested remediation (if known)

You should receive a response within 48 hours. If you do not, please follow up on the same channel.

docs.title: Supported Versions
docs.text: Security updates are only provided for the latest released version. Please always use the latest version available.

docs.title: Disclosure Policy
docs.text:
• You will receive an acknowledgment of your report within 48 hours.
  • We will investigate the issue and determine its impact and severity.
  • We will fix the issue in a future release and credit you if you wish to be credited.
  • We ask that you do not publicly disclose the vulnerability until we have published a fix and given users time to update.

docs.title: Security Best Practices
docs.text:
• Keep everything up to date.
  • Do not expose admin interfaces directly to the internet without a reverse proxy and proper authentication.
  • Use strong, unique passwords and enable multi-factor authentication where available.

docs.title: 1. Setup
docs.text: Prepare the package, development tools and documentation environment.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Make, Bash, Git and uv on Linux, macOS or Windows with Git Bash/WSL. uv uses or provisions a Python interpreter; run make install-uv if uv is missing.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/AmineDjeghri/python-package-template.git
cd python-package-template
make install-dev
make pre-commit   # static checks and hooks
make test-all     # tests
make docs-build   # strict documentation build

make check runs all three at once (and first warns if the Git hooks are missing).

This creates .venv, installs the editable package, the development/docs tools and, in a Git checkout, the Git hooks, then validates the checkout. No integration service or credentials are needed. Optionally copy .env.example to .env to customize settings such as LOGGING_LEVEL.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
make run

This runs the greeting example.

docs.title: Documentation site
docs.text: make deploy-doc-local

docs.title: Everyday commands
docs.text: Command Use make check The full local gate before a pull request make test-local Self-contained tests only make pre-commit Run the static hooks; FILES="path/a path/b" limits them to files make docs-build Strict documentation build make deploy-doc-local Preview the documentation site make clean Remove caches and temporary files make help List all targets

docs.title: Optional environments and tools
docs.text:
Command Use make install-prod Production dependencies only make install-tools Quality and docs tools without the application dependencies make install-release Packaging and release tools without the application dependencies make update-uv Update an existing uv installation make act Run GitHub Actions locally (make install-act first; needs Docker and .env) make docker-build Build the development image make docker-dev Open a container with this project mounted in /app make docker-prod Open a shell in the built image

The Dockerfile currently calls make install-dev without first installing uv; install uv in the image before that step to use these Docker targets. Inside the container, use make run and make check. docker-dev uses a separate volume for /app/.venv. A manually managed environment can use uv pip install -e .; that alone does not install the development tools. For publication, see release credentials.

docs.title: Editor and agent rules
docs.text:
Select .venv/bin/python; mark src as Sources Root and tests as Test Sources Root. Follow .editorconfig for indentation and line endings. Agent rules live in AGENTS.md; CLAUDE.md links to it for Claude Code. Edit AGENTS.md to update the shared instructions.

make help lists all targets. Next: Conventions and Testing.

docs.title: 2. Project structure
docs.text: Where things are, and where to add yours.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
src/python_package_template/
  example.py            example module, console script `hello`
  settings.py           ApplicationSettings (pydantic-settings) and the loguru logger
tests/
  README.md             test map and commands
  unit/                 self-contained package tests
    docs/               API reference generation
    release/            artifacts, release guards and upload recovery
docs/
  developer/            this guide
  examples/             example scripts, rendered as pages by scripts/gen_example_pages.py
  images/               logo and screenshots
scripts/
  emoji_commit_parser.py  semantic-release parser that accepts a leading emoji
  gen_doc_stubs.py        API reference pages from package/workspace source directories
  release_artifacts.py    Git release tags and complete wheel/sdist checks
  gen_example_pages.py    pages from docs/examples/*.py
makefiles/              one .mk per concern, included by Makefile
.github/                workflows, composite actions, Renovate, issue and PR templates
Dockerfile              development / production container
properdocs.yml          documentation site (MkDocs Material)
CHANGELOG.md            written by semantic-release, never by hand

docs.title: Where to add things
docs.text: Task Where Help a module src/python_package_template/<module>.py and tests/unit/test_<module>.py Add a module a setting settings.py Add a setting an example docs/examples/<name>.py Add an example a make target makefiles/<concern>.mk with a ## description —

docs.title: Add a setting
docs.text:
1. Add a field to ApplicationSettings in settings.py:

    EXAMPLE_ENDPOINT: Optional[str] = Field(default=None, description="the endpoint")
EXAMPLE_API_KEY: Optional[SecretStr] = Field(default=None, description="the api key")

  2. Set it by environment variable or .env; add it, empty or with a safe default, to .env.example.

  3. Secrets are SecretStr: read them with .get_secret_value(); they print as **********.

docs.title: Add a module
docs.text:
1. Add src/python_package_template/<module>.py, with Google-style docstrings: they become the API reference page automatically.
  2. Add tests/unit/test_<module>.py, or use a responsibility subfolder for tooling tests.
  3. Log with the package logger: from python_package_template.settings import logger.

docs.title: Add an example
docs.text: Drop a .py file in docs/examples/. Its module docstring becomes the description on the Examples page.

docs.title: 3. Conventions
docs.text: The rules every change follows.

docs.title: Code
docs.text:
• Use the make targets (make help): CI runs the same ones.
  • Docstrings on public functions and classes (Google style): they generate the API reference.
  • Settings through ApplicationSettings (settings.py, pydantic-settings), not os.environ scattered in the code.

  • Logging with the package's loguru logger, not print:

    from python_package_template.settings import logger

logger.info("Loaded {} items", count)

  • Log, then raise; do not swallow exceptions:

    if not path.exists():
    logger.error(f"File not found: {path}. Current directory: {Path.cwd()}")
    raise FileNotFoundError(path)

    In an except block, logger.exception(...) logs the message and the stack trace. Not raising is fine only when a loop must go on after one failure.

  • Large data: Polars. CPU-bound work: multiprocessing pool map.

docs.title: Branches and pull requests
docs.text:
1. Comment on (or create) the issue and wait to be assigned.
  2. Branch off dev: feature/<name> or bugfix/<name>. Stay up to date with git merge dev (branch already pushed) or git rebase dev (local only).
  3. Run make check (4. Testing), then open a pull request to dev. Its title follows the commit convention below: it becomes the squash commit and decides the version.
  4. When dev is ready, a pull request dev → main releases it.
  5. After a release, merge main back into dev (merge commit, direct push). On conflicts on CHANGELOG.md or a pyproject.toml version, keep main's and regenerate uv.lock with uv lock.
Merge Strategy Why feature/* → dev squash one conventional commit per feature dev → main squash one commit for semantic-release to evaluate main → dev (sync) merge commit, direct push syncs stable metadata; [skip ci] in the release commit prevents a spurious RC

Never edit a version in pyproject.toml or create a tag by hand: semantic-release does both.

docs.title: Commit convention
docs.text:
[emoji] <type>[(<scope>)][!]: <description>, the emoji is optional (Gitmoji).

Emoji Type Aliases Release 🐛 fix bugfix, hotfix patch ⚡️ perf patch ✨ feat feature minor 💥 feat! BREAKING CHANGE: footer major ♻️ 📝 🎨 🧪 🔧 👷 📦 refactor, docs, style, test, chore, ci, build none

A ! or a BREAKING CHANGE: footer makes any allowed type a breaking change (major release).

✨ feat(auth): add GitHub App token rotation
🐛 fix(llm): handle empty response from the API
💥 feat!(api): remove the v1 endpoint

feat(auth): redesign token flow

BREAKING CHANGE: /v1/token removed, use /v2/auth instead

On dev, a releasable commit increments the release-candidate counter (1.1.0-rc.1 → 1.1.0-rc.2) unless a larger bump is needed (for example, a breaking change → 2.0.0-rc.1 when the last stable release was 1.0.0).

Scopes are optional. Common scopes: ci, deps, docs. The commit message is checked on commit (commitizen) and the pull request title by ci.yml.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
• Never write a credential to a file of the repository, even untracked: use environment variables or .env (git-ignored).
  • detect-secrets runs on commit. For a line that intentionally references a secret placeholder (${{ secrets.X }}), add # pragma: allowlist secret. File-level exclusions in .pre-commit-config.yaml only for recurring false positives; never exclude a whole workflow to silence one line.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: Adding, renaming or removing one, in the same change: the setting in settings.py, .env.example, and the workflow env: if CI needs it.

docs.title: Dependencies (Renovate)
docs.text:
Renovate (.github/renovate.json5) applies a 7-day cooldown to Python dependency, GitHub Actions, pre-commit and tracked Node updates. Python runtime/Docker updates require dependency dashboard approval and have no configured cooldown. Security fixes bypass grouping, cooldowns and dashboard approval. Runtime PyPI dependencies use ranges; dev/docs dependencies use exact pins in pyproject.toml. uv.lock locks the resolved versions. Review every Renovate pull request before merging; after merging one, wait for the others to rebase.

  1. The current requires-python range is >=3.12,<=3.14.8. Keep all package manifests aligned and write code compatible with Python 3.12; CI runs make test-all on Python 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14.8.
  2. Renovate is configured to propose widening requires-python after dependency dashboard approval, preserving the 3.12 minimum. Python Docker updates share the runtime update group and also require approval; review all project constraints and update the CI matrix by hand when needed.
  3. PyPI updates use strict Python compatibility filtering. Weekly lockfile maintenance refreshes versions already permitted by dependency ranges; review the lockfile and CI results too.
  4. Renovate updates dependency files, GitHub Actions and pre-commit revisions; update README and developer documentation when the supported Python range changes. Docs are not rewritten automatically.
  5. Renovate tracks the Node pin in default_language_version, which every Node-based hook uses. Stable updates wait seven days and use chore; major upgrades open as normal pull requests labelled needs-compatibility-review.

docs.title: 4. Testing
docs.text: Run all existing software tests and static/documentation checks.

docs.title: Before a pull request
docs.text:
Complete setup, then run the three checks:

make pre-commit   # static checks and hooks
make test-all     # tests
make docs-build   # strict documentation build

make check runs all three at once (and first warns if the Git hooks are missing):

make check

All current tests are self-contained; there is no integration suite or coverage instrumentation yet. test-all runs the unit tests, then builds the wheel and loads its entry point in an isolated environment. Future integration suites must join test-all and CI.

docs.title: Focused checks
docs.text:
Command Scope make check pre-commit-status, pre-commit, test-all and docs-build make test-all Unit tests plus the built-wheel smoke; required comprehensive check make test-unit / make test-local Unit tests; use ARGS to select cases make test-installation Build the wheel, install it in a throwaway env, load hello make pre-commit Static hooks and strict docs; FILES="path/a path/b" selects files make pre-commit-status Warn when the Git hooks are not installed make docs-build Strict docs build only make build-package Build and verify the wheel/sdist separately

For example:

make test-unit N=1 ARGS="-k release"

Tests use four workers by default (N=4). test-all rejects selection filters; empty collections fail. make test-installation builds the wheel and loads its entry point in an isolated environment; test-all runs it after the unit tests.

docs.title: Writing tests
docs.text: Use tests/unit/test_<module>.py; tests/README.md maps docs/release tests. Use tmp_path and monkeypatch so parallel tests share no state or local dotenv settings. Mark async tests with @pytest.mark.asyncio (strict mode). Release tests use isolated Git/GitHub/uv command substitutes and never publish.

docs.title: CI
docs.text: CI and both release branches run static checks and test-all; summaries include setup failures. Build/package installation checks remain separate, and no live-service validation is claimed.

docs.title: Static and documentation hooks
docs.text: Hooks check formatting and lint (Ruff), syntax and whitespace, secrets, Markdown and spelling, the lockfile and the strict docs build, workflow syntax (actionlint) and workflow security (zizmor). Commitizen runs only at the commit-msg stage. make install-dev installs the Git hooks in a checkout (not in CI or Docker); run make pre-commit-install if that step failed, and make pre-commit-status (part of make check) warns when they are missing. make pre-commit only runs the hooks and never installs them. See .pre-commit-config.yaml for the full list; pip-audit, bandit and markdown-link-check are disabled. .github/zizmor.yml holds the one zizmor exception: the release workflow's checkouts keep their credentials because they push.

docs.title: 5. Release
docs.text: Publish the package to a GitHub Release (one wheel and one sdist, never a package index) and the documentation to GitHub Pages.

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
• Before you start
  • What a release does
  • Automatic release (CI)
  • Manual release (local)
  • Recover an interrupted release
  • Verify the release
  • Fix a bad release
  • After a release: sync main into dev

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Once, in the repository settings:

  • Actions → General → Workflow permissions: Read and write. The workflow declares permissions: {} and grants contents: read to the checks, contents: write to the release and docs jobs.
  • Pages → Deploy from a branch → gh-pages.
  • Squash merging enabled, so the PR title decides the version (commit convention); set the default squash commit message to the PR title.

Locally, install the tooling and log in:

make install-dev
gh auth login

Credentials resolve from GH_TOKEN (environment or local .env), then the token saved by gh auth login, then a hidden terminal prompt; release-assets uses the token or gh login, and CI supplies its automatic token. Never print credentials. A tooling-only environment can use make install-release; docs need make install-tools or make install-dev.

docs.title: What a release does
docs.text:
1. Validate the source (the guard; in CI, HEAD must also equal the tested GITHUB_SHA).
  2. Version with semantic-release from Conventional Commits. Its build hook builds and checks the package before anything is committed, tagged or published.
  3. Commit, tag and push chore(release): v<version> [skip ci].
  4. Upload the wheel and sdist to the GitHub Release.
  5. Deploy docs from the release tag, on a stable main release only.

Never edit a version, the changelog or a tag by hand. All workspace package versions equal the root version; tags keep vX.Y.Z-rc.N spelling, Python artifact names use X.Y.ZrcN.

flowchart TD
    PUSH["push to main/dev · dispatch"] --> SKIP{"[skip ci] in<br/>head commit?"}
    SKIP -- yes --> NONE["nothing runs"]
    SKIP -- no --> QC["quality-checks<br/>pre-commit + make test-all<br/>(contents: read)"]
    QC -- fail --> NONE
    QC -- pass --> VER["make release-version<br/>main/dev · clean tree · in sync<br/>tested-tip check"]
    VER --> HOOK["build hook<br/>uv lock --upgrade-package + make build-package<br/>failure stops everything"]
    HOOK --> NEW{"new version?"}
    NEW -- no --> SUM["outcome step: nothing published"]
    NEW -- yes --> TAG["commit + tag + push<br/>chore(release) [skip ci]<br/>gh release create"]
    TAG --> RETRY{"release already<br/>complete?"}
    RETRY -- "retrying" --> BUILD["make build-package"]
    RETRY -- no --> UP
    BUILD --> UP["make release-assets<br/>tag at HEAD · wheel+sdist<br/>--clobber"]
    UP --> MAIN{"main?"}
    MAIN -- "dev (rc)" --> DONE["release candidate published"]
    MAIN -- yes --> DOCS["docs job: checkout the tag<br/>install tools · make deploy-doc-gh"]

docs.title: Automatic release (CI)
docs.text:
release.yml runs on every push to main or dev, and on manual dispatch:

Branch Result dev release candidate vX.Y.Z-rc.N, marked prerelease main stable vX.Y.Z, and docs deployed from that tag

quality-checks is the gate (quality-and-tests.yml: pre-commit, then make test-all); if it fails or is skipped, nothing is versioned or published. The release commit carries [skip ci], so its own push does not re-run the gate. A retry accepts that exact single-parent chore(release) child of the tested commit and rejects any newer application change.

Docs-only commits bump no version, so they publish nothing.

docs.title: Manual release (local)
docs.text:
Use a clean main (stable) or dev (candidate), synchronized with origin. Complete setup and Before you start, then run:

make check
make release

The release command versions, builds and uploads the wheel/sdist set. It changes Git and GitHub; coding agents need explicit per-action approval.

docs.title: The guard
docs.text:
The release refuses unless the branch is main or dev, the tree is clean and HEAD equals origin/<branch>. make release-status reports these without changing anything; run it when a release refuses.

  • Dirty tree: commit it first as chore(...); a fix:/feat: commit becomes part of the release and bumps the version.
  • Not in sync: git pull --rebase when behind, git push when ahead.
  • Wrong branch: release from main (stable) or dev (candidate) only.

For a stable manual release, publish docs separately from the clean released tag:

make deploy-doc-gh

That command pushes gh-pages and requires separate authorization.

docs.title: Recover an interrupted release
docs.text:
Each stage is re-runnable and stops before publishing on a bad precondition:

  • make release-version requires main/dev, a clean tree and HEAD equal to origin, and in CI rejects a branch that advanced past GITHUB_SHA.
  • The semantic-release build hook runs uv lock --upgrade-package "$PACKAGE_NAME", stages the lock and builds the package; a failure stops the run before any commit, tag or publication.
  • make release-assets requires the tag at HEAD and the wheel/sdist pair.

make release chains them, reuses valid artifacts, builds missing ones and uploads sequentially.

Pick the smallest retry that matches the state:

  • CI: rerun the failed job while its tested source still matches the release.
  • Same branch, locally: make release stops without uploading when nothing is left to publish.
  • From a clean checkout of the exact tag: make build-package, then make release-assets.
  • Newer application commits exist: let their own workflow release them. Never rebuild an older release from later source.
  • release-assets can create a missing GitHub release and replaces same-named attachments (--clobber); it does not publish to a package index.

docs.title: Verify the release
docs.text:
• gh release view vX.Y.Z --json assets,isDraft lists one wheel and one sdist, with isDraft: false.
  • git rev-parse vX.Y.Z^{commit} is the chore(release): vX.Y.Z [skip ci] commit.
  • CHANGELOG.md carries the entry semantic-release wrote.
  • Stable only: gh-pages has a new commit and the site shows the new version.

docs.title: Fix a bad release
docs.text:
• Fix forward: revert on main and let the next patch release carry the fix.
  • Do not move, delete or re-create a published tag: both asset targets require the tag to point at the checkout being published, and artifact names derive from the version.

docs.title: After a release: sync main into dev
docs.text: Merge main back into dev after a stable release. Use the stable version and changelog as the base for the next candidate; see branch conventions.

docs.title: 6. Fork
docs.text: Start a new Python package from this repository.

docs.title: Rename
docs.text:
What Where distribution name, description pyproject.toml: [project] name, description package folder src/python_package_template/, imports, and [project.scripts] entry points console script pyproject.toml: [project.scripts] (hello) logger name settings.py: the name used to bind and filter the loguru logger Docker image name makefiles/docker.mk: CONTAINER_NAME documentation README.md, AGENTS.md (CLAUDE.md links to it), properdocs.yml, SECURITY.md, docs/ version and changelog semantic-release owns project.version and CHANGELOG.md; never edit them by hand

Then: uv lock, make install-dev, make check.

docs.title: Once on GitHub
docs.text:
1. Create main and dev, and protect them; use squash merges for pull requests. Allow release automation and the documented main → dev merge sync to push as needed.
  2. Workflow permissions "Read and write", and GitHub Pages from gh-pages (5. Release).
  3. Install the Renovate app on the repository.

docs.title: Stay in sync with upstream
docs.text:
Shared files: makefiles/, Makefile, scripts/emoji_commit_parser.py, .pre-commit-config.yaml, .markdownlint-cli2.yaml, .github/, docs/developer/.

git remote add upstream https://github.com/AmineDjeghri/python-package-template.git
git fetch upstream
git checkout upstream/main -- makefiles/release.mk   # the files you want
git diff --staged                                     # review before committing

class ApplicationSettings(BaseSettings):
    """Configuration for python-package-template.

    Values are read from environment variables and optionally
    overridden by a ``.env`` file.
    """

    # if .env is present, it will override the environment variables
    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file=".env", extra="ignore")

    # use .get_secret_value() to get the value
    EXAMPLE_API_KEY: Optional[SecretStr] = Field(default=None, description="the api key")
    EXAMPLE_ENDPOINT: Optional[str] = Field(default=None, description="the endpoint")

    logging_level: str = Field(
        default="DEBUG",
        validation_alias=AliasChoices("LOGGING_LEVEL", "logging_level"),
        description="Log level (TRACE, DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL)",
    )

    def model_post_init(self, __context):
        """Called after model initialization."""
        pass

docs.title: Run checks
docs.text:
1. Prepare the locked development tools with make install-dev.
  2. Run make test-all for every existing software test, using four pytest workers by default.
  3. Run make pre-commit for static hooks and strict docs, or make check for hooks and software tests.
  4. Use make docs-build independently when checking documentation.
  5. Run make build-package separately when artifact inputs change; synthetic test artifacts do not prove a real wheel installs or runs.

make test-unit ARGS="-k release" selects a focused diagnostic run. make test-all rejects filters. Release tests execute isolated command substitutes; they never publish or mutate this checkout. Package tests import settings from temporary working directories and do not load local credentials.

There is no integration suite yet. Add tests/integration/ and include its real tests in make test-all when one exists. Report coverage and artifact/runtime checks separately; coverage instrumentation is not currently configured. See the testing guide.
